messages.author: a53b84328fe123a8
messages.subject: stan error messages under OSX Mountain Lion vs Ubuntu
parts:
Hi Stan team,

I'm trying to dig into an issue that a user had a while back, but which did not get resolved. The main problem is, when I run my stan model on mac OSX the error messages are not informative. The same exact code spits out decipherable error messages on Linux.  

Compare this:
(OSX 10.8.4, R 3.0.1, RStan 1.3.0, Rcpp_0.10.4, g++ 4.8.1)

TRANSLATING MODEL 'LTLhfit2' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW.
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 
  c++ exception (unknown reason)
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

To: 
(Ubuntu 13.04, g++ 4.7.3)

TRANSLATING MODEL 'LTLhfit2' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW.
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : 
  INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=0; lower bound=1; upper bound=9; index position=2; Stim
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done 

 Any thoughts on what might be the cause of this? Have other users experienced this problem? 

Thanks in advance,
Angela

On 1/30/14, 6:57 PM, David Chudzicki (dch...@gmail.com) wrote:
> I'm not sure if my problem is connected with Angela's, but I'm on OSX getting the same message so maybe this thread is

> "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
> Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Covariance matrixCovariance matrix is not positive
> definite. Covariance matrix(0,0) is 1.0595482065447281e-176:0."

No, that's not going to be be connected with that error. I'm still
wondering what we should do about the informational message here because
it's really confusing users no matter how much we qualify it.

I'm not sure what's going on here. We are fixing a problem that
reported similar errors when (log) gamma functions underflowed/overflowed
and we weren't catching the specific type of exception they threw from
the Boost C++ library.

Your Windows environment reports:

OS: x86_64, mingw32; rstan: 2.1.0; Rcpp: 0.10.6; inline: 0.3.13

so I'm wondering if you're using a 32-bit version of R on Windows?

Can you share the model and data that's causing a problem on OS X?

> P.S. Having recently installed RStan on both OSX and Windows, I'm really impressed with how clear/easy-to-follow the
> installation instructions are for both systems. That was very nice.

Thanks. We try, but the way R's set up behind the scenes makes it
very fiddly --- there's no way to do a binary install in R (that we
know of, anyway) that doesn't mess with R's global configuration.
Therefore, the install depends on whatever else may have been installed
beforehand and what config those installs may have left behind. Having
users have to edit global files seems very suboptimal.

And we're always happy to hear where the instructions are confusing
and even happier to field proposed corrections.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan error messages under OSX Mountain Lion vs Ubuntu
parts:
I'm attaching the code and data. The R code with the problematic call
to Stan is "gp-fit.R".

This is the same as the Stan GP example on Github
(https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/develop/src/models/misc/gaussian-process),
except that I switched a line in gp-fit.R to load the data from
gp-fit-data.R. (This doesn't make a difference to the outcome.)

Also, a new clue: I've just gotten a new computer with a fresh install
of everything, and everything works fine. The same model fits with no
problem. I wonder if the problem was related to having installed R
with brew previously -- installing R with brew is a big mistake (lots
of things don't work), and I had quickly uninstalled it and installed
from the binary. But I may have left a bunch of the dependencies that
brew installed with it hanging around, which could have messed up some
compiler settings or something. Just a guess.

So: I still get the same errors on the old computer, but everything is
fine on the new one. Let me know if you'd like me to do anything on
the old one to help diagnose things. If that would be helpful, it'd be
easiest for me if we do it in the next week or so, as I'm likely to
give the old one to someone else at work.

(To clarify: I didn't think the informational message was signaling a
real problem, although explaining it to other people might be a pain,
and it does make the console look ugly, so I can definitely see that
handling the situation another way could be nice if you think of a
good one.)

-David

parts:
Hi Stan team, 

Just installed on Mac OSX 10.9.1
R 3.0.2 with 
RStan 2.1.0, 
Rcpp 0.11.0
inline 0.3.8

tried to run 

DD <- list(N = length(TC), y = TC, x1=Q, x2=p1,x3=p2,x4=p3)
stan.code <- 'data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real x1[N];
  real x2[N];
  real x3[N];
  real x4[N];
  real y[N];
}
parameters {
  real beta0;
  real beta1;
  real beta2;
  real beta3;
  real beta4;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
} model {
  for (n in 1:N)
    y[n] ~ normal(beta0 + beta1 * x1[n] + beta2 * x2[n] + beta3 * x3[n] + beta4 * x4[n], sigma);
}'

olsSTAN <- stan(model_code = stan.code, data = DD, 
                iter = 1000, chains = 1)

and got error:

Error: index out of bounds
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

Tried some old stan files which used to work and getting the same message. Though I would share in my concern.

On Wednesday, July 31, 2013 10:41:24 PM UTC-4, Angela Radulescu wrote:
Hi Stan team,

I'm trying to dig into an issue that a user had a while back, but which did not get resolved. The main problem is, when I run my stan model on mac OSX the error messages are not informative. The same exact code spits out decipherable error messages on Linux.

COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW.
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW (CHAIN 1).

  c++ exception (unknown reason)
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

TRANSLATING MODEL 'LTLhfit2' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'LTLhfit2' NOW.

 Any thoughts on what might be the cause of this? Have other users experienced this problem? 

Thanks in advance,
Angela
